entity: New Mexico Department of Game and Fish
stance_basis: endorses Executive Order 11644 implementation as beneficial to wildlife while urging application of guidelines to state lands and participation in planning meetings
summary: The New Mexico Department of Game and Fish reviewed the Draft Environmental Statement and endorsed implementation of Executive Order 11644 as beneficial to wildlife, citing long-standing concern about ORV impacts on hunting, fishing, and wildlife disturbance. The Department expressed concurrence that federal ORV guidelines could be applied to state lands and requested participation in meetings to discuss this, while detailing existing state-level restrictions they had already implemented.
complaint_summary: The New Mexico Department of Game and Fish endorses implementation of Executive Order 11644 as beneficial to wildlife, expresses long-standing concern about ORV impacts on wildlife and hunting, concurs that federal guidelines should extend to state lands, and requests participation in planning meetings, while listing seven existing state-level ORV restrictions already in place.

statement.text:
We have reviewed the Draft Environmental Statement prepared by the Bureau of Outdoor Recreation, Department of the Interior, proposing Department implementation of Executive Order 11644, pertaining to use of off-road vehicles on public lands.
The statement is well prepared and adequately presents the impacts on wildlife. We endorse the implementation of Executive Order 11644 as it should be beneficial to wildlife.
The Department of Game and Fish has long been concerned with off-road vehicle travel as it pertains to hunting and fishing and to disturbance of wildlife. Reasons for this concern are reflected on pages 13, 14, 15, and 16 in the statement under the discussion of Physical and Biologic Impacts.
We are in concurrence with you that guidelines for off-road vehicles as proposed by the Bureau of Outdoor Recreation for federal lands could be applied to our state lands and we would welcome the opportunity to participate in a meeting to discuss this.
For your information actions that we have taken concerning off-road vehicle travel is presented below:
1. During the antelope hunts, no vehicle bearing an antelope hunter may be driven off established roads in the hunting locality; provided, however, that a vehicle may be used to

retrieve legally taken and tagged game. This has been a regulation for many years. A large percentage of state lands are involved in the antelope hunts.
We have restricted off-road vehicle travel and in some cases all vehicle travel on Department-owned lands. This restriction has prevented damage to vegetative cover, and in particular, has increased hunter success because of less disturbance to the game animals.
3. This year our Commission passed a new regulation which prohibits driving off established roads while hunting on state lands.
4. Another new regulation makes it unlawful to use vehicles on any roads that the Forest Service has posted as closed to vehicular traffic.
5. We have worked closely with the Forest Service, Bureau of Land Management and local livestock boards to discourage off-road vehicle use, primarily through publicity.
6. A law, 40A-15-1, Criminal Damage to Property, has been sparingly used by us to file complaints where off-road vehicles have caused damage to vegetative cover. A regulation that could be applied to off-road vehicles, makes it unlawful to use a motor-driven vehicle to pursue, harass, harry, drive, rally or take game mammals or game birds.
7. Our Department is enforcing the recent Snowmobile Act that has made operators of snowmobiles aware of their side affects and that they have certain responsibilities.
